items.answer: Two things. First, a notch calculator helper: the analyst gives a previous and a current rating and gets back the notch change and the resulting WL (REQ-06-02). Second, the Indicator 12 (Country rating change) WL, worked out from the notch change (REQ-03-12). Success means the contract functions return the values set by REQ-03-12 and C1-C3, C6. Worked examples: BBB+ -> BB+ is a 3-notch downgrade with calculator WL=2. BBB+ -> BBB- gives 2 notches and WL=1. A 1-notch downgrade gives calculator WL=0 and Ind. 12 WL=1. A 2+ notch downgrade gives Ind. 12 WL=2. Upgrades and unchanged ratings give WL=0. Other parts of the POC will import these functions.

items.answer: Yes, concrete examples exist for everything except one field. Ind. 12: 1-notch downgrade -> 1; 2+ notches -> 2; upgrade or unchanged -> 0 (REQ-03-12, C3). Calculator WL: 1 notch -> 0 (C6); 2 -> 1 (BBB+ -> BBB-); 3+ -> 2 (BBB+ -> BB+); upgrade or unchanged -> 0 (C2, C3, C6). notchChange: positive = downgrade, negative = upgrade, 0 = unchanged (Contract). Input: ' bbb+ ' is the same as 'BBB+'; anything else -> RangeError (C1). The exception: notchCalculator().notches for an upgrade has no value that can be tested yet, because its sign is not specified. That is tracked as the open item CON-interface, and ACs for that field wait on its answer.

items.answer: Every contradiction is settled by the request itself. (1) The REQ-06-02 example 'BBB+ -> BB+ = 2 notch downgrade -> WL=1' miscounts. C2 overrides it: 3 notches -> WL=2, and BBB+ -> BBB- = 2 notches -> WL=1. (2) The calculator thresholds (Ind. 13: 2 -> 1, 3+ -> 2) differ from the Ind. 12 thresholds (1 -> 1, 2+ -> 2). C2 and C6 settle it: the calculator uses Ind. 13, Ind. 12 keeps its own, and a 1-notch downgrade gives calculator WL 0 but Ind. 12 WL 1. (3) 'Pre-filled from public source' is out per C4. (4) 'Auto-filled value editable' is met by the contract per C7. (5) 'Displayed' is met by the returned object per C8. (6) 'tests ... next to the code under test/': repo convention test/<area>/<name>.test.mjs applies (CLAUDE.md, README). The sign of notchCalculator().notches is a gap, not a contradiction. See CON-interface.

items.question: What sign does notchCalculator(previous, current).notches carry for an upgrade? The two readings: it is the signed 'notch change' (REQ-06-02 wording, same as notchChange), or it is a magnitude, with the separate `direction` field carrying the sign.
options: A. Signed, identical to notchChange(previous, current): BBB+ -> BB+ gives { notches: 3, direction: 'downgrade', wl: 2 }; BBB- -> BBB+ gives { notches: -2, direction: 'upgrade', wl: 0 }; unchanged gives notches 0.

B. Unsigned magnitude (always >= 0), direction carries the sign: BBB+ -> BB+ gives { notches: 3, direction: 'downgrade', wl: 2 }; BBB- -> BBB+ gives { notches: 2, direction: 'upgrade', wl: 0 }; unchanged gives notches 0.
items.impact: This is a public contract that other POC parts import and render ('N-notch upgrade'). With A, renderers must take the absolute value, and notches duplicates notchChange. With B, callers who need the signed value call notchChange, and notches matches the request's own phrasing ('3-notch downgrade'). Downgrades, unchanged, wl and direction are the same under both options. Only the upgrade value of notches changes, plus every AC and test that asserts it. Choosing wrong breaks consumers or forces a contract change later.

history.answer: Settled parts (for reference). RATING_SCALE = the 19 ratings of C1, best first. notchChange(previous, current) -> integer, positive = downgrade, negative = upgrade, 0 = unchanged (= index(current) - index(previous) on RATING_SCALE). notchCalculator(previous, current) -> { notches, direction: 'downgrade'|'upgrade'|'unchanged', wl }, where wl is 0|1|2 (Ind. 13 thresholds per C2, C3, C6). countryRatingChangeWl(previous, current) -> 0|1|2 (REQ-03-12, C3). Inputs are strings, trimmed and case-insensitive (C1). Not settled: the sign of notches.

items.answer: Any previous or current value that, once trimmed and upper-cased, is not one of the 19 ratings in C1 makes the function throw a RangeError. Taken literally ('anything else'), this covers: unknown ratings ('CC', 'D', 'NR'), empty or whitespace-only strings (''), inner spaces ('BBB +'), and non-string values (null, undefined, 42). It applies to notchChange, notchCalculator and countryRatingChangeWl. The last two are built on the same validation, so the RangeError reaches the caller unchanged. There are no fallbacks, no default values and no error codes. Message wording is not specified (see X-error-message).

items.question: Should the exported RATING_SCALE be immutable (frozen) so a consumer cannot change the scale that notchChange relies on?
options: A. Export Object.freeze([...19 ratings]). Mutation is ignored, or throws in strict-mode ESM, and the contents stay exactly the C1 list.
B. Export a plain array. notchChange uses its own private copy, so changing the export does not affect calculations.
C. Export a plain array that notchChange uses directly. Simplest, but a consumer mutation would corrupt results.
items.impact: Internal robustness only. Contents, order and the export name are fixed by C1 and the Contract under every option. Recommended: A. QA may add a test that the scale cannot be modified.

items.question: What should the RangeError message say for invalid ratings? C1 fixes only the error type.
options: A. Name the offending argument and value, and list the valid ratings (e.g. 'Invalid rating for previous: "CC". Expected one of AAA, AA+, ..., CCC-').
B. Name the offending value only (e.g. 'Unknown rating: "CC"').
C. Use a generic message ('Invalid rating'). Tests assert only the error type.
items.impact: No behavioural or contract effect: tests assert instanceof RangeError (C1), and messages may be checked with a loose regex at most. A or B makes analyst-entered typos easier to diagnose.
